model_specifications.PSharpP: Total decision languages in deterministic polynomial time with an oracle language in PP; equivalent to decision P^#P, not function #P or search PPP.
model_specifications.CH: Union over a fixed finite level k of C0=P and C[k+1]=PP^[Ck]; k is independent of input length.

facts.justification: A deterministic polynomial-time machine makes one query to its total PP language oracle.
A polynomial-length accepting-path count is reconstructed using polynomially many PP threshold queries; its parity decides the language.
P^PP⊆PP^PP is contained in the fixed second standard level of CH.
For every fixed level, enumerate counting branches and recursively answer oracle queries in polynomial space. The language chooses a fixed level and polynomial bound.

rules.justification: PP circuits give polynomial-size Boolean circuits for #P output bits by polynomially many threshold queries, with advice for all polynomial query lengths. Lemma3 then gives CH=MA. Its proof uses LFKN and PP^PH⊆P^PP; it does not assume GRH or infer CH collapse merely from P^PP=PP.

Fortnow–Rogers Theorem3.3 gives PP^AWPP=PP unconditionally. Induct on the fixed counting level, replacing only its oracle class using the hypothesis. No unrelativized outer-machine inclusion is relativized.
P^PP⊆P^PH⊆PH because each particular PH oracle has a fixed finite level. Induct using C[k]⊆PH ⇒ C[k+1]⊆PP^PH⊆P^PP⊆PH. The strengthened Toda theorem supplies the middle step.
Replace the PP oracle in P^PP and invoke the unconditional identity P^parityP=parityP. Only the oracle position is replaced.
Apply the existing length-regular polynomial padding from EXP to E, followed by polynomial-time many-one closure of PSharpP. For CH the simulated language has a fixed finite level.
Apply the existing length-regular polynomial padding from NEXP to NE, followed by polynomial-time many-one closure of PSharpP. For CH the simulated language has a fixed finite level.
Apply the existing length-regular polynomial padding from EXP to E, followed by polynomial-time many-one closure of CH. For CH the simulated language has a fixed finite level.
Apply the existing length-regular polynomial padding from NEXP to NE, followed by polynomial-time many-one closure of CH. For CH the simulated language has a fixed finite level.

complements.justification: Swap the deterministic oracle machine’s accepting and rejecting outcomes.
Every PP oracle level is complement closed by the standard integer-gap transformation; the fixed-level union is complement closed.

limitations: No promise/function/algebraic endpoint is implicitly identified with these total binary language classes.
